title: Unacademy Alternative for Educators (2026): Own Your Academy
description: For educators weighing teaching on Unacademy against their own academy: what Unacademy publishes, when staying fits, and how to start your own app on the side.
og_description: Unacademy is a large learning platform you teach on, not software you buy. A fair look at staying, building your own academy with your own app, or doing both, from official sources checked on 24 Oct 2026.
h1: Unacademy Alternative for Independent Educators (2026): Stay, Build Your Own Academy, or Do Both
dek: Unacademy is a large learning platform educators teach on, not software you subscribe to. Here is a fair comparison of your real options, using only what each side publishes on its own website.
cover_alt: Unacademy alternative for independent educators: stay on a big platform, build your own academy and app, or do both
audience: Independent educators in India who teach, or plan to teach, on large edtech platforms and are considering their own academy
intro: The Unacademy alternative for an independent educator is an academy of your own: your website on your own domain and your own Android app (iOS app on Pro or any yearly plan), where you set the price and keep the student list, built by you and, if your contract allows, run alongside your platform teaching. Unacademy describes itself as "India's largest online learning platform". For an educator it is a place to teach, not a tool you buy, so the honest comparison is between staying, building your own, or doing both.

A large platform gives an educator something hard to build alone: a big audience, a recognised brand and technology you never have to think about. Your own academy gives you a name, a price and a student relationship that stay with you. Both are real, and plenty of educators want some of each.

We are AllCoaching, the software for the second path, so read this knowing who wrote it. We quote only what Unacademy and the other brands publish on their own websites, checked on 24 Oct 2026, and we say where staying is the better choice.
takeaways: Unacademy is a learning platform, not academy software: it calls itself "India's largest online learning platform"; educators teach on it rather than buying a plan.
Unacademy does not publish educator pay, revenue share or terms on its website; unacademy.com/educators showed the homepage when we checked on 24 Oct 2026.
Staying brings reach and a recognised brand; your own academy brings your own name, price and student list. Many educators do both.
Read your contract before you teach elsewhere. Look for exclusivity and content-ownership clauses, and ask the platform in writing or a lawyer if anything is unclear.
Being "your own Unacademy" is possible at your own scale: live classes, recorded courses, tests and notes in your own app, without its audience on day one.
AllCoaching's monthly plans (₹3,999, ₹5,999 or ₹7,999 a month) take 0% commission, or Starter costs ₹6,999 a year + 10% on sales, GST extra, after a 7-day free trial with no card needed.
At ₹1.5 lakh of sales a year, your own academy costs ₹21,999 on Starter before GST.

sections.h2: The short answer: decide what you want to own
sections.html:
The best Unacademy alternative depends on what you want to own. If you want your own brand, app and student list, build your own academy. If you want a large audience and are happy teaching under a platform's name, staying can be the right call. Many independent educators do both.

{{fig:verdict|Unacademy alternative by need: own app and student list, your own academy on AllCoaching; large audience under a known brand, stay on Unacademy; reach and your own name, do both; audience first, YouTube|Find the row that matches what you want next.}}

The rest of this guide explains each path, what is and is not published, and how to start your own academy without giving anything up first.

sections.h2: How we compared Unacademy with your own academy
sections.html:
We compared the paths on what decides an independent educator's next five years.

  1. Reach on day one: how many students can find you.
  2. Brand: whose name students remember.
  3. Price: who decides what a course or batch costs.
  4. Student relationship: whether you can reach your students directly.
  5. Income: a payout on someone else's terms, or your own sales minus costs.
  6. Effort: what you have to run yourself.

For Unacademy, Physics Wallah and Vedantu we used only their own websites. "Not published" means the official website did not say, not that the term does not exist.

Disclosure: AllCoaching publishes this guide, and we sell academy software, so we have an interest in the answer. Unacademy publishes no educator terms that we could find, so we describe it only in its own words. Every outside figure links to an official page and carries the date we checked it (24 Oct 2026). Terms change; check the source before you decide. If you spot an error, write to contact@allcoaching.in and we will correct it.

sections.h2: Why educators look for an Unacademy alternative
sections.html:
Educators who look for an Unacademy alternative are usually not complaining about the platform. They want a business that carries their own name. The reasons tend to fall into a few groups.

What a large platform does well

Unacademy calls itself "India's largest online learning platform".[1] A platform of that size can put a capable educator in front of more students than most could reach alone, with an app, payments and support already built. For an educator who wants to teach and nothing else, that is a fair and valuable offer.

1. Wanting your own name to grow

On a large platform, students often find the platform first and the educator second. Educators who want students to search for them by name, and follow them wherever they teach, start building their own academy.

2. Wanting to set your own price

Your own academy lets you price a UPSC answer-writing programme, a GATE mechanical test series or a CUET English batch the way you think is fair, and change it when you want.

3. Wanting to reach your students directly

When you launch something new, you want to tell the students who already trust you. On your own academy, the student list is yours and exportable.

{{q:Can I be my own Unacademy?|Yes, at your own scale. You can run live classes, recorded courses, test series and notes in an app with your name on it. What you will not have on day one is a large platform's audience, so plan how students will find you: your YouTube channel, Instagram, WhatsApp and search.}}

4. Wanting one place for everything

Educators who grow a following on YouTube often end up with classes on one app, notes in Drive links and fees on UPI screenshots. One academy login replaces that.

{{fig:before-after|Before and after for an independent educator: live class on YouTube, notes in Drive links, fees on UPI screenshots, doubts in WhatsApp groups, mocks on Google Forms, compared with one academy login with your own website, app, live classes, checkout and tests|Whatever you decide about Unacademy, your own students deserve one home.}}

2. Keep teaching on Unacademy

Good at
Reach. It describes itself as "India's largest online learning platform", with exam preparation across many categories.[1]
Published pay or terms
Not published. unacademy.com/educators showed the homepage, and we found no educator terms page (checked 24 Oct 2026).
Free trial
Not applicable: you teach on the platform rather than buying a plan.
Check
Your agreement: exclusivity, who owns the classes you record, and whether you may teach or sell elsewhere.
Best for
Educators who value a large audience and a known brand more than owning the business.

3. Teach for another edtech brand

Good at
Physics Wallah describes itself as an "affordable and comprehensive learning experience" for JEE, NEET and classes 6–12;[2] Vedantu calls itself "the top choice for LIVE online classes for K1 to K12".[3]
Published pay or terms
Physics Wallah: not published. Vedantu publishes earning claims on its become-a-teacher page; they are Vedantu's claims, not a revenue share.[3]
Check
The same contract questions, plus any fixed availability hours.
Best for
Educators who like the big-brand model but want a different exam or format. See our Physics Wallah alternative guide.

4. YouTube and WhatsApp only

Good at
Building an audience. A YouTube channel is free to start and many Indian educators grow there first.
Published price
Free to start.
Check
Selling a course, collecting fees and running tests means stitching several tools together.
Best for
Educators still building an audience. When viewers start asking how to buy, read how to turn your YouTube channel into your own app.

5. Another academy platform

Good at
Classplus, Learnyst, Graphy and others also let you sell under your own name.
Published price
Varies by platform; we compared their published prices, with sources, in our Classplus alternatives guide.
Check
Yearly price, fee on sales, whose developer account the app sits under, and whether you can set it up yourself.
Best for
Educators who need a feature a particular platform is known for, such as a heavy test engine.

sections.h2: What your own academy costs as you grow
sections.html:
A fair money comparison with Unacademy is not possible, because Unacademy does not publish what it pays educators. We will not estimate it. What we can show is what your own academy costs at different sales levels, from AllCoaching's published prices.

  • ₹1 lakh of sales a year: ₹16,999 for the year on Starter (plan price + fee on sales, before GST).
  • ₹3 lakh of sales a year: ₹35,499 for the year on Growth yearly (₹12,999 + 7.5% fee on sales, before GST).
  • ₹5 lakh of sales a year: ₹47,988 for the year on Starter monthly (₹3,999 a month, 0% commission, before GST).
  • ₹10 lakh of sales a year: ₹47,988 for the year on Starter monthly (₹3,999 a month, 0% commission, before GST).

Each figure uses whichever plan costs least at that level (illustrative, before GST): yearly Starter (₹6,999 + 10%) at low sales, yearly Growth (₹12,999 + 7.5%) from about ₹2.4 lakh, and monthly Starter at 0% commission (₹3,999 a month, ₹47,988 a year, no sales limit) from about ₹4.7 lakh, where every further sale is 100% yours. The yearly plans are Starter ₹6,999 + 10%, Growth ₹12,999 + 7.5% and Pro ₹24,999 + 5%; the monthly plans (₹3,999, ₹5,999 or ₹7,999 a month) take 0% commission, with no lock-in and no sales limit. Payment-gateway charges on student payments are separate.

An illustrative example: a ₹1,500 JEE Main test series sold to 100 students is ₹1.5 lakh of sales. On Starter, the year costs ₹21,999 before GST. Your price and numbers will differ.

Remember the trade when you compare: on a platform, students come to you; on your own academy, you bring them.

{{cta}}

UPSC or state PSC educator with a loyal following

Answer-writing programmes and mains test series sell well under a teacher's own name. Your own academy fits. See online UPSC coaching platforms for educators.

NEET or JEE educator early in your career

A large platform can give you reach and practice teaching big batches. Build a small academy on the side, if your agreement allows, so your name grows too.

Niche exam educator (GATE, CUET, CLAT)

Niche exams reward depth, and students search for specialists. Your own academy lets you go deep. Read online GATE coaching or online CUET coaching.

Educator who wants to stay and diversify

Keep teaching on the platform and add one product of your own, such as a revision course. Start with how to sell courses online in India.

faq: What is the best Unacademy alternative for an independent educator?

For an educator who wants their own brand and student list, the alternative is your own academy. AllCoaching gives every plan a website on your own domain and your own Android app (iOS app on Pro or any yearly plan), with 0% commission on every monthly plan from ₹3,999 a month, or yearly from ₹6,999 plus a 10% fee on sales, GST extra, after a 7-day free trial. If you mainly want reach, staying on a large platform can suit you better.
Can I be my own Unacademy?

Yes, at your own scale. You can run live classes, recorded courses, tests and notes in your own app under your own name. You will not have a large platform's audience on day one, so plan how students will find you.
Unacademy does not publish educator pay, revenue share or terms on its website; unacademy.com/educators showed the homepage when we checked on 24 Oct 2026. Ask for the terms in writing.
Reach. It describes itself as India's largest online learning platform, so it can put an educator in front of a large audience with technology and payments already built.
Can I teach on Unacademy and run my own academy?
It depends on your agreement. Read it for exclusivity and content-ownership clauses, and ask the platform in writing or a lawyer if anything is unclear. This guide is not legal advice.
Will I lose reach if I teach independently?

At first, usually yes. Your own academy starts with your own followers. You grow it through YouTube, Instagram, WhatsApp and search, and AllCoaching also lists your courses on its marketplace app for discovery.
Can I bring my YouTube followers to my own app?

Yes. Put your academy link in video descriptions and pinned comments, offer a free demo lesson, and share the link in your WhatsApp community. Your website and app carry your name, so followers recognise them.
Is AllCoaching only for exam coaching?
No. Exam educators (UPSC, NEET, JEE, SSC, banking) use it, and so do skill educators teaching yoga, spoken English, music or coding.
